key_points: Minions are Stripe's homegrown coding agents — fully unattended, built to one-shot tasks
Over 1,000 PRs merged weekly are minion-produced, human-reviewed, with no human-written code
Typical run starts in Slack message, ends in CI-passing PR ready for human review
Engineers spin up multiple minions in parallel for parallel task completion
Built on forked Goose (Block's coding agent) with customized orchestration
Uses 'blueprints' — hybrid of deterministic code nodes and agentic LLM loops
Devboxes spin up in 10 seconds with pre-loaded code and services

competitors.title: How Stripe's Minions Ship 1,300 PRs a Week
key_points: 1,300+ PRs per week with zero human-written code

angles: Infrastructure over model: Why Stripe's decade of developer productivity investment made Minions possible — the walls matter more than the LLM

Blueprint architecture: The hybrid deterministic-agentic orchestration pattern that prevents LLM variance from breaking production
Enterprise governance lessons: How Stripe's safety layers (isolation, retry limits, human review, blue-green deploys) make 1,300 AI PRs/week manageable

outline: Introduction: The Slack emoji that ships code — how Stripe engineers trigger 1,300 AI-written PRs weekly
What Are Minions? — Defining unattended coding agents vs attended tools (Cursor, Claude Code)
The Origin Story: Why Stripe built its own — forking Goose, the uncommon Ruby/Sorbet stack, and the trillion-dollar codebase constraint
Architecture Deep Dive: The six infrastructure layers that make Minions production-grade
4.1 Devboxes: Isolated, ephemeral, 10-second provision from warm pool
4.3 Toolshed: 400+ MCP tools with scoped access per task
4.4 Three-tier feedback loop: Local lint → selective CI → full CI (max 2 rounds)
4.5 Agent rule files: Scoped, conditional, shared with human-operated tools
4.6 Hard retry limits: Preventing runaway costs and infinite loops
The Developer Experience: From Slack emoji to CI-passing PR — the frictionless workflow
What Minions Excels At (And What It Doesn't): Configuration, dependency upgrades, flaky tests vs novel features, architectural decisions
The Industry Context: Google (30%+ AI code), GitHub Copilot (90% Fortune 100), Meta's mid-level engineer AI
The Governance Gap: 80.9% deploying agents, 14.4% with security approval — CVE-2025-53773 and the safety imperative
Stripe's Safety Architecture: Isolation, human review, blue-green deploys, scoped tooling as a reference model
The Future: Non-engineers shipping code, machine-to-machine payments, agent-native businesses
Key Takeaways for Engineering Leaders: Invest in infrastructure, not just models — the walls matter more than the LLM
Conclusion: From vibe coding to production-grade autonomous agents — the blueprint for agent-native engineering
